q: Compare this month to the same number of days last month.

answer:
By order date (sales, orders, profit) and native ad delivery date (ad spend): this month-to-date (1–29 Oct) vs the same 29 days in Sep shows higher topline and traffic but deeper losses — net sales rose to ₹17,85,040 (+17.9%), orders to 965 (+7.1%), while net profit worsened from -₹2,85,039 to -₹3,23,189 (worse by ₹38,150, -13.4%); ad spend rose to ₹13,74,235 (+18.7%) and net ROAS moved slightly from 0.7537 to 0.7648 (+1.5%).

What changed, and why it matters:
- Net sales up 17.9% (Sep ₹15,13,540 → Oct ₹17,85,040): more revenue, so marketing is driving volume.
- Ad spend up 18.7% (Sep ₹11,57,266 → Oct ₹13,74,235): spend grew slightly faster than sales, which explains why profit did not improve.
- Orders up 7.1% (901 → 965): conversion volume rose, but average economics weakened enough that net profit is more negative.
- Net ROAS slightly higher (0.7537 → 0.7648, +1.5%) but not enough to offset the absolute increase in ad spend and the deeper loss per order.

Worth checking: split the change in ad spend and ROAS by ad platform and campaign to see which campaigns scaled spend without profitable returns.
